label: Roadside
description: Machine-culture places off the tarmac — pullouts, workshops and stops where riders and drivers actually gather.

items.name: pass-summit-pullout
items.text: A gravel pullout at a mountain pass summit, the elevation sign crusted with faded stickers, valley haze stacked in blue layers below.
items.text_short: mountain pass pullout, stickered elevation sign

items.name: desert-diner
items.text: A chrome-trimmed desert diner on a dusty gravel lot, screen door propped open, power lines sagging away toward the heat-blurred horizon.

items.name: workshop-doorway
items.text: The open roller door of a back-street workshop, tool chests and a two-post lift in the shadows behind, sunlight cutting a clean line across the oil-stained threshold.

items.name: coastal-layby
items.text: A layby on a coastal switchback, a low drystone wall between the tarmac and the drop, surf glittering far below the guardrail posts.

items.name: old-filling-station
items.text: A preserved 1950s filling station, round-top pumps and enamel signs under a slim cantilevered canopy, oil bottles racked by the office door.

items.name: logging-spur
items.text: A gravel logging spur through cathedral firs, mist drifting between the trunks, a fresh berm of graded stone along the verge.

items.name: river-quay
items.text: A cobbled river quay with iron mooring bollards, stone bridge arches upstream and houseboats breathing smoke across the water.

items.name: riders-cafe
items.text: The car park of a legendary riders' cafe, helmets hung on mirrors, mugs steaming on the window ledge, decades of club stickers layered on the door glass.
items.text_short: riders' cafe car park, helmets on mirrors

items.name: salt-flat-camp
items.text: A cracked white salt flat running to the curvature of the earth, a canvas awning and fuel drums making a small camp under an enormous sky.
items.text_short: salt flat camp, endless white pan

items.name: paddy-switchbacks
items.text: A narrow road switchbacking between terraced rice paddies, each flooded terrace holding its own mirror of the sky.
